It is hard-snapped to integers, implying a caret that hops in whole-pixel jumps rather than easing between columns — and at 74px tall (100% of the 74px line pitch, ~2.4x the ~30px ascender height) those two square corners park a blunt 6px blue brick 21px above the ascenders, in empty leading.
gapTheirs: A's caret is 0.2px off the pixel grid and blurred on both flanks: outer columns render at 80% coverage (x=357) and 20% (x=363) instead of B's uniform 100% across all six columns, so only 4px of the 6px bar is full-strength. Worse, that 20% cyan fringe lands on x=363 — the first ink column of the 'a' — tinting the letterform, where B holds a clean 0-bleed boundary against grid-snapped glyphs.
verdict: These are the same caret — 6px wide, 74px tall, #00BFFF, same 357-362 slot — and the only real decision either app made is what happens at the ends. A drew its caret: 3px caps, subpixel placement, the signature of a bar that can ease between positions instead of teleporting. B took the free rectangle, and pays for it with two hard corners floating in the leading above every line. Both of you shipped a caret 2.4x the ascender height and 24% of the character cell in unmodified CSS DeepSkyBlue, flush against the 'a' with zero right clearance — that is the defect a writer actually sees at 1x, and neither of you fixed it.

states.gapTheirs: Draws TWO carets — identical 6px×76px #00B5FF bars at x=910 and x=1404, bracketing the selection — so nothing indicates which end is live; and #00B5FF is the only saturated pixel in an otherwise pure-greyscale document (text #1C1C1C, markers #9E9F9F, bg #F9F9F9), at 3 CSS px wide and 2.45× cap-height (76px caret vs 31px cap) it is a fence post, not a nib
states.verdict: A's caret is loud and doubled — a 3px electric-cyan slab at each end of the selection, the brightest thing on a page that is otherwise pure grey, and it tells you nothing about direction because both ends look identical. But it exists, it is exactly co-extensive with the selection band (both y458–533, zero px mismatch), and you can find it from across the room. B hands you a pale block of highlight and no cursor whatsoever; a writing surface where the insertion point can vanish entirely is not a precise instrument, it is a guess. Present-and-vulgar beats absent.
